REAL CHEM II is a comprehensive course that delves into chemical kinetics, equilibria, acids and bases, and various reaction classes. The course begins by exploring the factors influencing reaction rates, mechanisms, and quantitative techniques for determining reaction rates. It then covers chemical equilibrium, including concepts such as equilibrium constants, Le Châtelier's principle, and equilibrium calculations.

The course examines acids and bases, discussing their definitions, measurements, strengths, and roles in acid-base equilibria. It also covers buffers, which resist changes in pH, and titrations, a key analytical technique in chemistry.

The course further explores the equilibria of other reaction classes, including solubility and complex ion equilibria. It delves into thermodynamics, focusing on the second law of thermodynamics and Gibbs free energy.

Throughout the course, students will develop a deep understanding of chemical reactions, their underlying principles, and their applications in various fields, from environmental science to industrial processes. They will also gain proficiency in performing calculations related to reaction rates, equilibria, acids and bases, and thermodynamics, enhancing their ability to analyze and predict quantitative aspects of chemical reactions.
